title: AWS account boundary (hard isolation unit)
hook: An AWS account is the strongest default isolation boundary in AWS. Resources, billing, service quotas, and most security policies are scoped to a single 12-digit account ID.

blocks.text: Every AWS account is a separate container with its own Identity and Access Management (IAM) namespace, default service quotas, billing records, and resource ARN prefix (arn:aws:service:region:account-id:resource). You cannot share a VPC across accounts without explicit peering or AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM). Multi-account strategies use separate accounts for dev, staging, production, security tooling, and log archive to limit blast radius.

entries.plainDefinition: A unique 12-digit number identifying your AWS account in ARNs and cross-account trust.
The email owner of the account with unrestricted access — avoid daily use.
entries.example: Enable MFA on root; use IAM users/roles for operations.

entries.plainDefinition: How much damage one mistake or breach can cause.
entries.example: Separate prod account limits dev misconfiguration impact.

blocks.text: Interviewers test whether you understand accounts as security and billing cells, not just login credentials. A compromised access key in a shared account endangers every environment. Landing zone patterns provision dedicated accounts per workload or environment under AWS Organizations.

blocks.title: Interview one-liner
blocks.body: Account = hard boundary for IAM, billing, and quotas. Split environments across accounts before relying on tags alone.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Management account
items.body: AWS Organizations root; consolidated billing; SCP attachment point.

items.title: Workload accounts
items.body: Separate prod, staging, dev with distinct IAM and quotas.

items.title: Security account
items.body: Central CloudTrail, GuardDuty, Security Hub aggregation.

items.title: Cross-account access
items.body: IAM roles with trust policies — never long-lived keys in every account.

snippet.label: CLI: get caller identity and list accounts
snippet.code:
aws sts get-caller-identity
# Account, Arn, UserId

aws organizations list-accounts \
  --query 'Accounts[].{Name:Name,Id:Id,Status:Status}' --output table
snippet.explanation: get-caller-identity confirms which account your credentials target. list-accounts shows the org structure.

snippet.label: CloudFormation: cross-account role trust
snippet.code:
Resources:
  CrossAccountDeployRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: cicd-deploy-prod
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/cicd-runner
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                sts:ExternalId: unique-deploy-secret
snippet.explanation: Prod account trusts CI account role with ExternalId condition — cross-account without duplicating users.

snippet.label: CLI: assume role into another account
snippet.explanation: Temporary credentials scoped to the target account role — preferred over static keys per account.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Running prod and dev in one account with only tag separation. Using root access keys for automation. Creating cross-account roles without ExternalId or condition keys.

interviewTakeaways: An AWS account is a hard isolation unit for IAM, billing, quotas, and ARNs.
Multi-account landing zones limit blast radius — split prod from non-prod at account level.
Cross-account access uses IAM role trust with temporary credentials, not duplicated long-lived keys.
60s: Account = security and billing cell. Org management account for consolidated billing and SCPs. Prod/dev in separate accounts. AssumeRole for cross-account with ExternalId.
Follow-up: how does AWS Control Tower automate landing zone setup?
commonPitfalls: Relying on tags alone for prod/dev separation — tags do not stop IAM mistakes in the same account.
Strong answer: separate accounts for environments; tags for cost attribution within accounts.
Storing root access keys in CI pipelines.
Trust policies with Principal: '*' and no conditions on cross-account roles.

jsTsCorrelations.note: Node apps using @aws-sdk/client-sts assume-role into target accounts per request. Hardcode account IDs in config, not in application code scattered across repos.
